incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Foreign-Invested Partnership is governed by the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China (2006 Revision), Articles 14, 15, 16, 62 and 63, together with the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2020), Articles 2, 30 and 31. Because the entity is a partnership rather than a company, the primary Companies Act is not applicable; the operative implementing instrument is the Administrative Regulations on the Registration of Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprises (SAMR Order, as revised in 2015), Articles 2 through 10.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Municipal or Provincial Market Supervision and Administration Bureau, Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration Office, at the FIP's principal place of business.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise, filed on the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Portal or in person at the authorized Market Supervision and Administration Bureau window.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under PRC partnership law. The partners are free to set contribution amounts in the partnership agreement. There is no minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement. Contributions may be made in cash, in kind, or by assignment of rights as agreed; foreign exchange contributions must be remitted through a SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital contribution account after foreign direct investment (FDI) registration, and actual contributions must be recorded in a capital contribution schedule filed with SAMR.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE EXECUTIVE MANAGEMENT BOARD OF [FIP NAME], A FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP

WHEREAS [FIP NAME] (the FIP) is a foreign-invested partnership registered under the Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China;

WHEREAS the FIP has no board of directors and is managed by its general partner or executive general partner under the partnership agreement;

WHEREAS the partners desire to adopt the internal governance measures necessary for the FIP to execute its air cargo charter brokerage and international freight forwarding business;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. The subscribed capital contributions set out in the executed partnership agreement and capital contribution schedule are ratified and approved. Each partner is directed to deliver the subscribed contribution to the FIP's designated bank account as scheduled. The executive general partner is authorized to issue capital contribution certificates, to record contributions in the statutory books, and to make all necessary filings with the State Administration for Market Regulation, the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, and the local tax authority.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office and principal place of business at [full address] is adopted as the statutory address of the FIP. The executive general partner is authorized to execute, deliver, and, if necessary, amend the premises lease, to accept service of process, and to notify the competent registry authority of any future change of address.

3. BANKING. The FIP shall open a RMB basic deposit account, a foreign exchange capital account, and such other accounts as may be required at [bank name]. The bankers are directed to honor instructions bearing the signatures of any two of the following authorized signatories: [name], [name], and [name]. SWIFT wire transfers and Fedwire transfers are expressly permitted, subject to the FIP's sanctions compliance and anti-money-laundering policies.

4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. The following officers are appointed for the FIP: [name] as Executive General Partner; [name] as Compliance Officer, responsible for anti-money-laundering, sanctions, and transport regulatory compliance; and [name] as Partnership Secretary, responsible for statutory filings, books and records, and corporate governance. Each officer is granted authority to execute all regulatory applications and to retain counsel, auditors, and bank agents as necessary.

5. COMMON SEAL. The common seal, if adopted, is approved. The seal shall be held by the Partnership Secretary and may be applied to documents only after approval recorded in the seal register.

6. RATIFICATION. All actions previously taken by the partners, counsel, and consultants in connection with the formation, name reservation, capital planning, and pre-licensing applications are ratified and confirmed.

7. EFFECTIVENESS. This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force and effect until amended by a subsequent resolution or by written consent of the partners in accordance with the partnership agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Negative-List Pre-Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Enterprise Registration Portal of the State Administration for Market Regulation and the local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit five proposed English or transliterated Chinese trade names on the SAMR enterprise registration portal, indicating that the applicant is a foreign-invested partnership. The application must include a Foreign Investment Negative List self-check and state that the proposed business scope is air cargo charter brokerage and international freight forwarding. The authority will search the enterprise name database for identical or confusingly similar names in the same industry. Upon approval, the system issues a name reservation notice valid for six months. Name reservation does not grant business authority but is a prerequisite for registration.
required_dossiers: Partners' identity documents, including foreign entity certificate of incorporation or passport
Foreign Investment Negative List self-check statement
Power of attorney for the authorized agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, add distinctive elements or amend the name and resubmit. If the negative-list screening flags the proposed air cargo brokerage scope, narrow the scope to non-restricted auxiliary activities or submit a compliance opinion confirming that the FIP will not operate an airline or own aircraft.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial or Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau, Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise through the SAMR online system or at the MSAB window. Foreign partner documents must be notarized, translated into English or Chinese by an authorized translator, and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate or apostilled if the investor is from a Hague Convention jurisdiction. For a Hong Kong corporate partner, provide a Hong Kong Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, and notarized incumbency certificate. The authority verifies the partnership agreement, capital contribution schedule, registered address, and executive partner information. On approval, SAMR issues the business license and unified social credit code.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Registration of a Foreign-Invested Partnership Enterprise
Foreign partner certificate of existence and good standing, apostilled or consular legalized
Identity documents of all Chinese and foreign partners
Proof of registered address, including lease, ownership title, and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a correction or supplementation notice, respond within 15 days with corrected forms, translations, or notarized documents. If registration is suspended because a foreign partner appears on a restricted or prohibited list, replace the partner or submit a formal negative-list compliance opinion. If notarization is deficient, re-execute before a notary and obtain fresh legalization or apostille before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, SAFE FDI Registration and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration local office; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) branch or delegated bank; commercial bank; and local General Administration of Customs office if import or export cargo handling is contemplated
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days after issuance of the business license, complete tax registration through the one-stop service, obtain a taxpayer identification number, and register for fiscal invoices in the logistics and transportation services category. Complete foreign direct investment registration with SAFE or a designated bank, open a RMB basic deposit account and a foreign exchange capital contribution account, and remit subscribed foreign contributions using the assigned foreign exchange reporting code. If the FIP will physically handle international cargo or file customs declarations, complete customs registration with the local customs office and obtain a customs registration code. The banking relationship must include an anti-money-laundering risk assessment reflecting the medium-risk air cargo charter brokerage sector.
required_dossiers: FDI information reporting and registration form
Bank account opening application and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAFE queries the source or use of funds, provide the underlying partnership agreement, capital contribution schedule, and bank source documents. If tax registration is delayed, file a written explanation with the tax office and pay any accrued administrative charges. If the bank requires additional know-your-client verification, provide beneficial ownership declarations, organizational charts, and projected transaction volumes for the air cargo brokerage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: International Freight Forwarding Recordal and Air Cargo Brokerage Eligibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) local commerce commission; Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) regional administrator for each charter flight; IATA or China Air Transport Association for voluntary cargo agency accreditation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the International Freight Forwarding Enterprise Recordal through the MOFCOM online filing system, selecting the business scope for air cargo forwarding and cargo aircraft charter brokerage. The FIP is not the aircraft operator; the actual carrier must hold a CAAC Air Operator Certificate. The FIP must verify charter contracts, aircraft insurance, traffic rights, and sanctions compliance. If the FIP seeks IATA cargo agency accreditation, submit the IATA Cargo Agency application and demonstrate qualifying sales volume and an approved compliance manual. Maintain a written anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance manual because banking partners classify this sector as medium risk.
required_dossiers: Business license and unified social credit code
International Freight Forwarding Recordal application form
List of senior officers and beneficial owners
Air cargo charter brokerage service agreement template
IATA or CATA accreditation application, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOFCOM rejects the recordal, correct the business scope to clarify that the FIP acts as an intermediary only and does not operate aircraft or warehouses. If CAAC requests charter approval, coordinate with the licensed airline to file a non-scheduled cargo charter application with traffic rights, insurance certificates, and the charter agreement, then resubmit within the prescribed comment period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety, Work Safety and Optional Physical Facility Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Emergency Management, Fire and Rescue Department; local Housing and Construction Bureau; Ecology and Environment Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an office-only FIP, complete the fire safety completion and acceptance filing with the local Fire and Rescue Department for the leased premises and maintain occupational safety records under the Work Safety Law. If the FIP later operates an air cargo warehouse, screening center, or ground handling facility, obtain a Civil Defense Fire Permit after fire design review and installation acceptance, obtain a structural load inspection report verifying floor capacity, and file a work-safety registration. If warehousing is added, submit an environmental registration filing to the Ecology and Environment Bureau before operation. This step is optional for pure brokerage but mandatory if physical handling or storage begins.
required_dossiers: Environmental registration form for warehouse use, if applicable
Hazardous waste handling contract, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire department issues a non-conformity notice, install required fire suppression and egress systems within the stated deadline and apply for re-inspection. If the environmental authority upgrades the classification from registration to a full environmental impact report, prepare and submit the full report to the Ecology and Environment Bureau and obtain approval before occupying the facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM), Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), and the local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau; for any physical cargo warehouse, also the Ministry of Emergency Management and the Ecology and Environment Bureau.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Freight Forwarding Enterprise Recordal; for air cargo charter brokerage, the FIP must contract with a CAAC-licensed airline and, as applicable, obtain IATA Cargo Agent Accreditation or China Air Transport Association cargo sales agency status. No separate air cargo sales agency license is issued by CAAC after the 2016 deregulation, but non-scheduled cargo charter flight approval must be obtained by the operating carrier from the CAAC regional administration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and the provincial or municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not applicable for a pure air cargo charter brokerage conducted from an office. The activity is an administrative service and is not a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehouse operation. If the FIP later adds a cargo warehouse, sorting facility, or ground handling station, a Category B Environmental Registration Filing is required; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required only for large-scale cargo terminals or hubs as classified by the MEE Catalogue of Environmental Impact Assessment for Construction Projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the brokerage-only model. For future warehousing or handling facilities, wastewater must meet the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard GB 8978-1996, fugitive volatile organic compounds and odors must meet GB 16297-1996 and applicable local emission limits, and hazardous waste such as contaminated packing, used oil, or degraded chemicals must be handled under a hazardous waste operating permit with MEE manifest and recordkeeping requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office-based FIPs must file fire safety completion acceptance with the local Fire and Rescue Department and maintain occupational safety compliance under the Work Safety Law. If the FIP operates a cargo warehouse or ground handling facility, it must obtain a Civil Defense Fire Permit or fire acceptance opinion, complete a structural load inspection for the storage area, and obtain work-safety pre-employment registrations before commencing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), electronic portal: China Electronic Tax Administration / National Unified Electronic Tax Service Platform (etax.chinatax.gov.cn); for Hong Kong SAR: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), electronic portal: eTAX (www.ird.gov.hk).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) formed in the People's Republic of China: first complete business registration with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory Tax Identification Number/TIN and VAT taxpayer ID for mainland China. Within 30 days of SAMR registration, file enterprise tax registration with the competent STA tax office through the integrated one-form/one-window procedure, supplying the partnership agreement, foreign investor identity and residency documents, registered address certificate, and declared business scope including air cargo charter brokerage. Through the same process, obtain VAT registration and the taxpayer status identification as a general VAT taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer. If a foreign non-resident partner has no permanent establishment or business presence in China, that foreign partner must be separately registered with the STA for non-resident withholding tax purposes and will receive a non-resident withholding taxpayer file number; this is a payer-side registration rather than an entity-level election. For any Hong Kong SAR nexus, a foreign non-resident entity carrying on business in Hong Kong must apply to the IRD for a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance within one month of commencement; the Business Registration Number (BRN) is the Hong Kong tax identifier, and profits tax follows the territorial source principle.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. PRC partnerships, including FIPs, are mandatorily transparent for enterprise income tax under Cai Shui [2008] No. 159; income is allocated to partners under the distribution-after-determination model, and the partnership itself is not an enterprise income tax taxpayer. The PRC and Hong Kong SAR tax systems do not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election for this FIP.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: PRC Value-Added Tax (VAT); Hong Kong SAR imposes no VAT, GST, or general sales tax (nil indirect tax regime).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover exemption from basic VAT registration: any taxable supply activity in mainland China requires VAT registration. The small-scale taxpayer monthly exemption threshold is CNY 100,000 (quarterly CNY 300,000), and mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration is triggered by annual taxable sales exceeding CNY 5,000,000. Hong Kong SAR has no indirect tax registration threshold because no VAT/GST/sales tax is levied.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: PRC VAT requires digital e-invoicing under the Golden Tax Phase IV system: VAT invoices are issued through tax-authorized software or the National Unified Electronic Invoice Service Platform, transmitted to the STA in real time, and stamped with an anti-fraud digital verification code; fully digitalized e-invoices require API-based integration with the STA and real-time fiscal clearance before issuance for high-volume taxpayers. Hong Kong SAR has no fiscal e-invoicing, real-time clearance, or digital stamping mandate.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The FIP may claim PRC export VAT zero-rating only if the taxable service is an international air cargo charter brokerage service supplied to a customer outside mainland China, the service is received and consumed entirely outside China, and the transaction is supported by contracts, actual outbound movement of cargo or aircraft, foreign-currency settlement through approved banks, and a compliant VAT/customs declaration. Under Cai Shui [2016] No. 36 and the STA cross-border taxable services administration, zero-rating or VAT exemption may apply depending on whether the charter brokerage is classified as a cross

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC), with delegated foreign-exchange administration to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE); the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) retains oversight of the Hong Kong dollar and HKD clearing systems.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese mainland operates a managed current-account convertibility system. Foreign-invested partnerships are permitted to remit operating revenues and partnership profit distributions offshore, but every transaction must be documented and booked through a designated foreign-exchange bank. Capital-account items such as foreign partner capital injections and external debt remain tightly controlled and require SAFE registration before the bank can debit or credit the relevant receipt/settlement accounts. There is no de facto convertibility for purely speculative flows. For an air-cargo charter broker, export freight service fees are current-account receipts: they may be retained in a foreign-currency settlement account or converted to RMB at negotiated rates, but the underlying invoices, charter-party agreements, load sheets, and airway bills must be archived and linked to the remittance. Profit distribution to the HK partner is permissible after audited accounts, tax clearance, and SAFE verification, but the receiving bank will conduct a spend-down and source-of-funds trace. In Hong Kong, the HKD is freely convertible under the HKMA Linked Exchange Rate regime; however, the mainland FIP remains the regulated treasury hub.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No fixed mandatory surrender ratio applies since the 2012 SAFE liberalization; export and service-trade foreign-currency receipts may be retained in a settling bank foreign-currency account or sold at negotiated rates. The statutory duty is repatriation into the PRC banking system: the FIP must credit the designated trade foreign-currency account, provide invoice, airway bill/charter-party evidence, and ensure each export receivable is collected within the commercial settlement term, for air cargo brokerage typically 30 to 90 days from invoice or uplift; overdue statuses beyond SAFE's monitoring threshold must be reported and explained.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational RMB and Foreign Currency Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow and Foreign Direct Investment Settlement Account
Export Proceeds Receipt Account and Air Charter Disbursement Account
Operating Current Account and Trade Payment Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally barred as a primary treasury rail for the mainland FIP. Foreign digital EMIs, including Airwallex, Wise, and Revolut, cannot maintain licensed RMB deposit or clearing accounts for a mainland foreign-invested partnership, and PBOC/SAFE rules prohibit enterprise cash management moving entirely outside designated foreign-exchange banks. Such EMIs may be used only as narrow bilateral receivables/payables tools in Hong Kong, not as the compliance ledger for the mainland entity, and all cross-border capital flows must still go through a licensed mainland bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person physical branch interview is mandatory for the mainland FIP. Under PBOC Customer Identification Procedures and SAFE account-opening practice, the managing partner/statutory agent and at least two authorized signatories must appear at a designated mainland branch with original registered documents, certified resolutions, company seals, and identification. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted for the mainland FIP; a Hong Kong-based partner may execute a notarized power of attorney and appear at an HK branch for documentary verification, but the mainland statutory agent still must complete face-to-face verification at the mainland bank before full functionality is enabled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Co-mingled freight forwarding commissions and aircraft charter disbursements across the HK and mainland entities with inconsistent supporting documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entity and UBO org chart, HK and mainland intercompany service agreements, monthly charter-party contract register, airway bill/invoice/booking-sheet three-way match, and transaction-level Excel reconciliation certified by the FIP managing partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived trade-based money laundering through inflated or unsettled charter brokerage fees between related principals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent charter market rate benchmarking, ICAO/IATA airway bill and aircraft registration evidence, pilot/log evidence for flown segments, published fuel and landing-fee schedules, and counter-party due-diligence files for every airline and cargo principal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership opacity caused by nominee shareholders or trust-like indirect interests from a high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE/PBOC-sanctioned UBO declaration, legalized passport copies of every 25% plus partner, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, multi-year audited financial statements, negative news and sanctions screening, and notarized confirmation that no undisclosed nominee arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of unlicensed payment service providers or offshore EMI accounts to bypass SAFE trade-repatriation monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete bank-statement trail from designated mainland FX settlement accounts, SAFE Goods/Services Trade Monitoring System registration codes, certificate of transaction classifications, and an external auditor confirmation that no customer or vendor payments were routed through unlicensed payment institutions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The HK partner must first complete MOFCOM/local market-supervision foreign-invested partnership establishment filing and obtain the SAFE foreign-exchange registration notice for the FIP before wiring. The remittance must be sent by SWIFT MT103 from the HK partner's corporate account to the FIP's capital escrow/settlement account in the designated mainland bank, using the SAFE-approved foreign-exchange purpose code for foreign-invested partnership capital contribution, not a service or goods code. After receipt, the bank debits/credits the capital-account settlement book, and if the funds are to be converted to RMB, settlement is completed under the bank's capital-item settlement authenticity review. A capital contribution certificate and a PRC-registered auditor's capital verification report, together with the receipted bank confirmation, must be retained; if the contribution is non-cash, an external valuation report and title-transfer evidence are required for future profit repatriation and tax basis.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for air-cargo charter brokerage, including aircraft charter deposits, freight prepayments, airport handling, and broker commissions, should be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV for direct correspondent clearing, with HKD/USD through HK Clearing House Automated Transfer System (CHATS) and Fedwire/CHIPS, and RMB cross-border settlements through CIPS. For high-value aircraft charter commitments, a Commercial Letter of Credit or standby LC (MT700/MT760) may be issued against the charter-party agreement, subject to bank credit approval. Documentary collections are generally unsuitable for time-sensitive charter disbursements and should be reserved for non-critical cargo logistics payments where invoice and airway bill presentation is required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Standard onshore CNY/USD and CNY/HKD forward contracts executed under SAFE real-demand documentation and trade/contract exposure evidence
Onshore foreign-exchange swaps and plain-vanilla FX options tailored to the actual charter-brokerage receivable/payable cycle, with no speculative net open position

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible for the HK treasury company only, not for the mainland FIP, and only when fully backed by verified HK business contracts and board-approved treasury policy
Cross-currency swaps permitted for eligible external debt/cross-border financing after SAFE registration, subject to the FIP's debt-to-equity ratio constraints

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Business Registration Certificate (Form BRC/R1) under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of the existing Business Registration Certificate; a one-month grace period is available only if the renewal application is lodged within 30 days after expiry.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a surcharge of HKD 300 per additional month; if renewal remains outstanding for 12 months, the registration may be administratively struck off and the general partner may be prosecuted for carrying on business without a valid registration, with fines up to HKD 10,000 plus daily default fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Partnership Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) together with partnership financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Profits Tax Unit, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month after the statutory issue date printed on the return; the general issue date for a March fiscal year end is 1 April, resulting in a general statutory filing deadline of 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Inland Revenue Department may raise an estimated assessment, impose a 10% additional tax on undercharged profits, and levy a late filing fine of up to HKD 10,000; persistent default can lead to prosecution and enforced collection action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form BIR56A) with individual employee returns (Forms BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the annual issue date, generally issued on 1 April for the preceding year of assessment, giving a standard deadline of 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is an offence carrying a maximum fine of HKD 10,000; knowingly untrue returns attract a penalty of HKD 10,000 plus treble the amount of tax undercharged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Air Cargo Charter Broker Aviation Enterprise Licence (air cargo broking and freight forwarding licence renewal under the Air Navigation Ordinance and applicable regulations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Civil Aviation Department, Air Transport Licensing Office, and Transport and Logistics Bureau as policy authority, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least 30 calendar days before the annual licence anniversary date; the renewal window opens 90 days before expiration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-renewal causes the licence to lapse on its anniversary date; carrying on air cargo charter broking after expiration is an offence attracting fines up to HKD 50,000 and imprisonment for six months, and reinstatement requires a full new application with compliance inspection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation Statement of Limited Partnership Registered Particulars (Partnership Annual Return / ACS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, Partnerships Unit, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after the anniversary of the partnership registration date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing fee of HKD 120 is imposed; if the confirmation statement remains unfiled for six months, the Companies Registry may initiate prosecution and administrative deregistration of the partnership.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Hong Kong-registered foreign-invested partnership (FIP), the Limited Partnerships Ordinance does not impose a blanket statutory audit. A certified independent CPA audit becomes legally or administratively mandatory where: (i) the Civil Aviation Department imposes an audited financial statements condition on the air cargo charter broker licence whenever annual broking turnover exceeds HKD 8,000,000 (approximately USD 1,025,641); (ii) the Inland Revenue Department issues a notice under section 51(1) of the Inland Revenue Ordinance requiring certified accounts, normally applied where gross business receipts exceed HKD 5,000,000 (approximately USD 641,026); (iii) total balance-sheet assets exceed HKD 2,000,000 (approximately USD 256,410) and simplified accounts are not available; (iv) average headcount exceeds 20 employees, in which case IRD normally requires accounts to be certified by a CPA; or (v) the partnership is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund with manageable assets exceeding HKD 30,000,000 (approximately USD 3,846,154) and the partnership agreement or fund regulations require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are fully converged with IFRS, constitute the applicable local GAAP; the HKFRS for Private Entities may be adopted for qualifying non-public-interest partnerships; tax computations remain subject to the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) and are reconciled from HKFRS-based accounting records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37) and Hong Kong AML requirements, the general partner must maintain an internal partner and beneficial-ownership register. Any admission, retirement, assignment, pledge, or change in the partnership distribution ratio must be notified to the Companies Registry on the prescribed amendment form within 30 calendar days of the event. There is no standalone annual UBO return for an ordinary HK limited partnership; however, the annual Business Registration Renewal and the Annual Confirmation Statement require the general partner to confirm controlling partner particulars as at the anniversary date. For limited partnership funds, notifiable changes must be filed within 14 days and the designated representative must annually confirm the fund's beneficial ownership structure to the Companies Registry.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (partnership equivalent of Register of Members)
Register of General Partners and Limited Partners (partnership equivalent of Register of Directors)
Register of Charges and Mortgages over Partnership Assets
Statutory Minute Book and Partnership Resolution Book
Significant Controllers / Beneficial Ownership Register maintained for AML record purposes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per audit engagement, depending on transactional complexity and licence conditions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 16.5% corporate profits tax (for corporate partners) / 15% standard rate for unincorporated individuals; the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) is treated as tax-transparent for Hong Kong Profits Tax purposes, with each partner being separately assessed.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No dividend withholding tax, no capital gains tax, no undistributed profits tax. Tax incentives include 100% deduction of qualifying research and development expenditure (300% deduction for first HK$2m and 200% for the excess), tax exemption for offshore profits in accordance with the territorial source principle, and profit tax exemption for qualifying aircraft lease management. For an air-cargo charter broker, the entity may claim a 100% deduction for charter-related operating expenses and depreciation (capital allowances) on eligible plant and machinery. There is no patent box. The Hong Kong-China Double Taxation Arrangement reduces withholding tax on qualifying cross-border payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: BIR52 – Profits Tax Return for Partnership Businesses (Inland Revenue Department, Form BIR52), filed through the IRD eTAX portal (https://www.etax.gov.hk) or by paper.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due within 1 month from the date of issue of the return (the "due date"). If the FIP appoints a Hong Kong tax representative, an automatic extension may apply; for accounting periods ending 31 December, the extended due date is usually 16 August of the following year; for periods ending 31 March, the due date is usually 15 November. A further extension may be granted on application to the Commissioner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Business name and Business Registration Number (BRN)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the legal name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) and its Hong Kong business registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the FIP has a non-resident general partner, still register with the BRC and state the name exactly as on the certificate. Non-HK identity numbers for partners should be indicated only where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Principal place of business in Hong Kong
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical office address where the central management and control of the charter-broking activity is exercised.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PO box alone is not acceptable. If the principal business is outside Hong Kong, mark this as "offshore operations relied upon" but such claim must be supported by evidence of contract negotiation and performance abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Business nature code (Hong Kong Standard Industrial Classification)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: HSIC code corresponding to the principal business activity: 5229 - Other transportation support activities (including air cargo forwarding and charter brokerage).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select HSIC 5229 and, if prompted, sub-classification 5229.02 for air cargo charter brokering. Misclassification may trigger an ISIC mismatch with China's customs and business registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Date of commencement and date of cessation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start date of the partnership business in Hong Kong; leave cessation blank if continuing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the FIP was formed in Hong Kong but all cargo-charter contracts are entered into overseas, the commencement date is still the date of business registration. Inconsistent dates across the PRC tax registration (confirmation date) and HK Inland Revenue Department file create a red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period covered by the return, normally the 12-month period ending at the business's annual account date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The basis period must match the audited financial statements. For a newly formed FIP, the first basis period cannot exceed 18 months. If the partnership claims a foreign-source income exemption, the basis period must still cover all contracts closed within the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Net profit / (loss) per prepared accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss before tax as shown in the audited or management accounts of the partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure must be reconciled with the PRC-partner contribution. Include all worldwide revenue if the partnership claims to be tax-resident in HK; if an offshore claim is made, only HK-source income is entered and the offshore part is segregated in supporting schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses that are capital in nature, private expenses, non-deductible entertainment, unpaid provisions and taxes imposed on income are added back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border management fees paid to the PRC parent must be added back unless the transfer-pricing documentation proves that the fee satisfies the arm's length principle and the benefits are actually enjoyed in HK.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Capital allowances and balancing charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for depreciation deductions under the Inland Revenue Ordinance in respect of machinery, plant, furniture and fixtures, and any balancing charges on disposal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The FIP must compute allowances separately for each partner's share if the partners are different taxpayers (e.g., individual vs corporate). A non-resident partner cannot claim HK capital allowances unless the asset is used to produce HK-source profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - Adjusted assessable profit / loss before allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The profit or loss after applying adjustments (Box 6 + disallowable expenses – capital allowances + balancing charges).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the FIP has mixed-source profits, the adjusted profit must be split between "Taxable Hong Kong profits" and "Offshore profits claimed exempt". A losing or lightly taxed FIP coupled with real economic activity offshore may still attract IRD enquiry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Share of adjusted assessable profit / loss attributable to each partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable profits or losses to each partner (by name and HKID/passport number) in accordance with the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Foreign-Invested Partnership with a PRC corporate partner, fill in the partner's share based on profit-sharing ratio, not capital contribution. The non-resident partner's share is not reduced by taxes paid in PRC – no foreign tax credit for HK profits tax is available against PRC tax unless there is a DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Losses brought forward from prior years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of unabsorbed trading losses brought forward from previous basis periods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unabsorbed trade losses may be carried forward indefinitely to be set against future profits, but only if the same trade continues. For a newly acquired FIP, a change in ownership or business may extinguish the carry-forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Provisional profits tax for the following year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of provisional tax payable is based on the current year's assessable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The provisional tax for a non-resident partner is based on the share of HK-source profits, not worldwide income. If the partnership makes a loss, no provisional tax is charged.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a fine of up to HK$10,000 plus a three-fold additional tax amount under section 82A for undercharged tax. The IRD may issue an estimated assessment, and failure to pay may lead to legal proceedings, asset freezing, and imprisonment up to six months for continued non-compliance. Where incorrect returns are filed with intent to evade tax, the maximum penalty is HK$50,000 (on summary conviction) plus imprisonment for up to three years and additional tax up to 300% of the tax undercharged.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Hong Kong does not impose dividend withholding tax on outbound distributions by a partnership or corporation; dividends are also not taxable in the hands of Hong Kong-resident recipients.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Hong Kong has no dividend WHT, no treaty relief application is required for dividends. For payments of interest or royalties to a resident of Mainland China, the Hong Kong FIP must (if withholding is nevertheless assessed under the Inland Revenue Ordinance for royalties deemed to be Hong Kong-source) protect the recipient by: (i) obtaining a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the IRD on Form IRC1314A; (ii) obtaining a beneficial ownership declaration and the recipient's PRC Tax Resident Certificate; (iii) submitting a DTA claim to the IRD before filing the BIR52, and if withholding is to be avoided in the source country (PRC), presenting the TRC and Form to the PRC tax bureau to apply the reduced rates under the China-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory HK deemed-profits withholding on royalties: for use of or right to use patents, trademarks, designs, copyright or similar property paid to a non-resident, 30% of the gross royalty is deemed assessable profit, giving an effective withholding tax of 4.95% (16.5% x 30%). For payments of interest to non-residents, there is no withholding tax in Hong Kong; however, if interest is derived from a Hong Kong trade or business, the non-resident may be liable to profits tax. Under the China-HK Arrangement, the maximum PRC withholding tax on royalties is 5% (or 3% for industrial, commercial or scientific equipment), and the maximum PRC withholding on interest is 7%, provided the recipient qualifies as the beneficial owner and obtains a HK tax resident certificate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Master File and Local File must be prepared by the Hong Kong FIP if it belongs to an MNE group whose consolidated group revenue in the prior accounting period exceeds HK$750 million (approximately US$96 million), and the FIP's aggregate related-party transactions exceed the following de minimis thresholds: goods – HK$88 million; financial transactions – HK$11 million; intangible property – HK$28 million; services – HK$22 million; other – HK$11 million. A Country-by-Country Report is additionally required if the group revenue exceeds HK$6.8 billion (or the equivalent of EUR 750 million). The FIP should also benchmark all charter-brokerage commission transactions with the PRC affiliate under the arm's length standard.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong has not enacted an Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but the territorial source principle imports a substance test: profits derived from air-cargo charter brokerage are taxable only if the core income-generating activities (CIGA) are performed in Hong Kong. The FIP must show that the negotiation, execution, performance, and invoicing functions are exercised in Hong Kong, or that the non-HK source position is supported by full documentation. The IRD may challenge a "paper FIP" by re-allocating profits under the transfer-pricing rules and the traditional anti-avoidance provisions (sections 61 and 61A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance). For purposes of the China-HK arrangement, central management and control (CMC) must be demonstrated to avoid double non-taxation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Foreign-Invested Partnership files a nil or offshore-exempt BIR52 for air-cargo charter brokerage commission that is in fact negotiated, contracted, and earned in Hong Kong, and fails to keep proper books or declares false consideration to the Collector.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue Ordinance (IRO) s.80(2) – upon conviction on indictment, a fine of HK$50,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years; under IRO s.82A, additional tax of up to 300% of the undercharged tax may be assessed. The IRD may also impose a daily penalty from the due date for non-filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: For a limited partnership, the general partner and any managing partner who signed or approved the false return are personally and jointly liable. The court may order civil asset restitution and a travel ban (blacklisting) under the IRO enforcement powers; directors of a corporate general partner may face disqualification, contempt of court, and criminal imprisonment up to 3 years for wilful tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP charges a zero or below arm's-length commission to its PRC affiliate for air-cargo charter brokerage services, fails to prepare Master File / Local File after exceeding the statutory thresholds, and retains no economic capacity (no employees or equipment) to support the services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRO s.50AAF – the IRD may adjust the assessable profits to an arm's length amount; s.51C – failure to keep sufficient records is a criminal offence, fine up to HK$100,000 and imprisonment up to 6 months; s.82A / s.80 – additional tax up to 300% of undercharged tax and penalties for intentional or negligent filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporate general partner is a shell, the court may pierce the partnership veil and hold its directors and shareholders personally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties. Directors may be jointly and severally liable under the tort of conspiracy, ordered to disgorge improper benefits, and subjected to a Hong Kong immigration restriction (travel ban) pursuant to a court order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Shell-Company / Failure to Maintain Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP operates as a pass-through conduit that collects charter-broker fees from the PRC parent via SWIFT/Fedwire and immediately distributes those payments as commissions or dividends to an offshore shell, without any local office, staff, board meetings, or AML/KYC documentation, and without keeping a beneficial-ownership register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) – failure to carry out customer due diligence or keep records: on conviction, a fine up to HK$1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years. Under IRO s.61 and s.61A, the arrangement may be void against the Commissioner; in China, the GAAR may be applied to recharacterise the transaction and impose penalty interest. The business may also be struck off and the air-cargo brokerage licence (if applicable) revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing partners who knowingly participate in a sham or use the FIP as a façade for fraud face civil liability for restitution, a worldwide asset freeze, travel restrictions (blacklisting by the IRD or courts), disqualification from acting as a director for up to 15 years, and criminal liability for money laundering or fraud involving imprisonment up to 14 years (under the Theft Ordinance and Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance).
